questions.q: Students who scored in the top 5% on a test's first attempt tend to score closer to the class average on an immediate retake, even with no change in ability or coaching. What best explains this?
choices: Regression to the mean: extreme scores partly reflect luck/noise, which is unlikely to repeat
It proves the top scorers cheated the first time
The retake is deliberately made harder
Top scorers get overconfident and stop trying

questions.q: Two people each bet their necktie on whose is cheaper, without knowing either value. Each reasons: 'If I lose, I lose my tie's value; if I win, I gain a tie worth more than mine — so this game favors me.' Both reason identically. Does this argument actually mean the game favors both players?
choices: No — it favors whoever proposed the bet
Yes — the game truly favors both, which is why it's called a paradox
No — the reasoning is flawed; by symmetry the game favors neither player
No — it favors whoever has the more expensive tie
